mathematical_input: Let f,g:R -> complex numbers be continuous and suppose they agree Lebesgue almost everywhere. Then f=g as functions. These are conditional representative inputs of this extract; continuity is not claimed for arbitrary L2 representatives.

source_steps.text: If the continuous functions disagreed at a point, continuity and the Hausdorff complex topology would give an open neighborhood on which they disagree. Every nonempty real open set has positive Lebesgue measure, contradicting almost-everywhere agreement. Thus they agree at every point, and function extensionality gives equality.
